challenge.title: Colonial Rule Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: six clue-and-conclusion decisions and four matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one activity. Get at least 7 correct to pass. All lesson clues are available even without saving them in your journal.

badge.name: Colonial History Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing all four Chapter 6 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes careful comparisons of authority, local responses, aims, methods and effects.

evidence.question: A report says Legazpi created Cebu and its history in 1565. Which clue directly checks that claim, and what conclusion fits?
choices: A Spanish base developed within a community that already had history
Cebu had no people or trade before 1565
A new settlement erased every earlier event
All islands instantly came under effective control
evidence.explanation: The existing-place clue explicitly identifies Cebu's earlier community, trade and leadership. A colonial development date does not mark the start of all local history.

evidence.question: A caption says geography alone created Manila trade. Choose the clue about regional participants and the conclusion it supports.
choices: Existing merchants and connections helped link newcomers to trade centered in Luzon
Location alone carried and exchanged every good
All Asian trade began with Spanish newcomers
A port guaranteed profit and universal consent
evidence.explanation: The regional-links clue identifies merchants' role in existing trade. A departure date and the meaning of tribute do not explain that trading connection.

evidence.question: Someone claims an issued order proves every distant community obeyed it. Which clue most directly tests actual reach?
choices: Check where and when the decision was carried out instead of assuming universal control
The order itself reveals every person's thoughts
A larger map label guarantees enforcement
A sponsor's wish proves the result
evidence.explanation: The careful-conclusion clue asks where and when a decision was carried out. Participant roles and a settlement date alone cannot establish universal enforcement.

evidence.question: A report places the Sulu treaty example in Legazpi's 1565 expedition. Which clue directly checks the period and what does it support?
choices: The Sulu example concerns a later 1726 treaty, not the 1565 expedition
Every treaty belongs to the same year as Legazpi's arrival
All communities made one identical decision
Diplomacy proves conflict never occurred
evidence.explanation: The later-Sulu clue explicitly places this example in 1726. Keep places and periods distinct instead of merging them with 1565.

evidence.question: A fictional sponsor wants trade access. Which clue about aims best supports the correct interpretation?
choices: Wanting access is an economic aim, not proof that it was achieved
A desired benefit is a guaranteed outcome
A motive automatically justifies coercion
A trade aim establishes everyone's consent
evidence.explanation: The economic-aims clue distinguishes what was sought from what was obtained. A 1565 event or a separate resistance record cannot prove this sponsor's result.

evidence.question: A payment record names one affected household. Which clue most directly checks a claim that every family had the same burden?
choices: Investigate who was affected in a particular place and time; do not invent a universal burden
One record establishes identical effects for all families
An official's aim reveals every family's feelings
A policy name supplies every household's circumstances
evidence.explanation: The people-and-evidence clue requires particular circumstances rather than a universal burden. Leadership roles and a city date address other questions.

matching.question: Match each part of the Legazpi investigation with its evidence.
pairs: A Spanish base in an existing community
San Pedro returned with navigators, captain and crew
matching.explanation: Departure, settlement and return are separate events. Recognize existing communities and shared work rather than crediting one person with everything.

matching.question: Match the comparison categories with the supported statement.
pairs: Local histories and leadership preceded those developments
matching.explanation: Colonial dates describe particular developments, not the beginning of all history or immediate control of every island.

matching.question: Match each local-response word with its meaning.
pairs: Changing some practices in response to circumstances
Opposing a demand or imposed authority
matching.explanation: These describe actions that can vary across people, issues and time. They are not permanent labels for every member of a community.

matching.question: Sort this fictional report by matching the aim, method and effect.
pairs: The example household had fewer goods afterward
matching.explanation: A desire, an action and an observed consequence are different categories. This fictional exercise does not establish every historical household's experience.
